subject: Boundary dossier: Dedicated & Private segmentation overview for SOC 2 review

Subject: Request: architecture summary and isolation mapping for SOC 2 walk-through

Hi Jonas,

As part of Brightline's SOC 2 scoping for next quarter, our auditors at SigmaAudit asked for a concise architecture packet showing how Redwood separates tenant workloads between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Specifically they're looking for: 

- A single-page boundary diagram per deployment mode that highlights control-plane vs data-plane demarcation.
- A short description of what is pinned to the customer VLAN/zone in Dedicated and what stays in Redwood-managed shared services.
- Any network ACLs, egress allowlists, and KMS partitioning notes relevant to tenant isolation.

Can you produce a brief dossier (diagram + 1–2 page narrative) and upload it to the Drive link below? Our auditor would like materials by EOD Wednesday PST if possible.

Thanks,
David

Hi David —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can put together a compact dossier that covers: high-level boundary diagrams (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), a succinct narrative describing control-plane/data-plane separation, where customer-managed networking sits for Private, and a short matrix showing services that run in tenant vnets vs Redwood shared services.

A couple quick clarifications so we scope correctly:
- Do you want separate diagrams for single-tenant Dedicated pools vs multi-tenant Dedicated (some customers reserve full pools, others share hardware)?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: architecture summary and isolation mapping for SOC 2 walk-through

David / Jonas —

Attached is the technical appendix I'm drafting (control-plane-separation.txt) and the initial service matrix. Highlights to call out in the dossier:

- Control plane (orchestration, model catalog, scheduling) is located in Redwood-managed control zones and communicates to Dedicated/Private compute over mutually authenticated mTLS channels. No customer data is stored in the control plane beyond metadata pointers to model versions.

- Dedicated: compute nodes can be configured in two modes:
  * Reserved pool (single-tenant): compute, network interface, and ephemeral storage are isolated to the customer VPC/VNet. Customer CIDR and BGP peering optional; egress is routed through a customer-provided firewall or Redwood-managed NAT with strict egress allowlists.
  * Shared-pool (multi-tenant): tenant workloads run on pinned CUDA instances with hypervisor-level isolation; network namespaces and VLANs are used to separate tenant traffic; control-plane commands are scoped per-tenant.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): customers run the Redwood runtime inside their VPC or on-prem appliances. We provide a lightweight agent that establishes a secure TLS tunnel to Redwood's control plane for telemetry and updates — customers can opt to air-gap updates if required.

- KMS: keys for customer data are either customer-managed (recommended for Private) or Redwood-managed with tenant-enterprise key scoping for Dedicated. We provide HSM-backed key wrapping where required.

I included an ACL example (lines showing only 443/22 for management, 1024-65535 ephemeral for data plane when needed) and a short egress allowlist template.

I will upload the Excel matrix (service-isolation-matrix.xlsx) with per-service columns: network boundary, allowed inbound, data-at-rest storage location, KMS ownership, and audit-log retention.

—Karthik

[Attachment stubs included: control-plane-separation.txt, service-isolation-matrix.xlsx]

Team —

This looks excellent. Two quick follow-ups from the SigmaAudit checklist: 
1) They want explicit statement on whether any cross-tenant admin APIs exist and how RBAC prevents tenant-scoped drift.
2) Confirmation that audit/logging retention for Dedicated deployments is configurable per-customer and that logs can be exported to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets.

If you can add 2–3 lines in the narrative addressing those points before you upload the packet, we should be good to hand these to the auditor.

Thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.

David

On Wed, Nov 3, 2027 at 07:45 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Uploading now to the Drive link. Attached: boundary-diagram-v2.png, control-plane-separation.txt, service-isolation-matrix.xlsx.
>
> Quick notes added to the narrative:
> - Cross-tenant admin APIs: none exposed that can access customer data across tenant boundaries. Administrative APIs are RBAC gated; operations require action tokens tied to an operator identity and are logged via our immutable audit stream.
> - Audit logs: retention defaults to 90 days for Hosted, configurable up to customer-specified retention (and export) for Dedicated and Private. Customers may configure log export to their own S3/GCS for long-term retention.
>

>
